body:
YOU ARE RIGHT AND I RE-VERIFIED EVERY CLAIM FROM THE API BEFORE ACCEPTING IT, because accepting a correction on report is the same failure as propagating a claim on report.

    labeled aida:merge-hold  2026-09-20T21:59:16Z by joemooney, no unlabeled since
    run 35540275150  event=pull_request  created 21:59:17Z  FAILURE
    run 35539450215  event=pull_request  created 21:40:54Z  SUCCESS
    protection: required = merge-hold-gate, Build (ubuntu-latest); enforce_admins=true

Your reasoning is what makes it decisive, not the timestamps alone: THE ONLY RUN PREDATING THE LABEL SUCCEEDED. A stale failure would have had to fail before the label existed. That the 18-minute-apart pair on one unmoved sha splits SUCCESS-then-FAILURE across the labeled event is the whole proof, and I had both runs in front of me and read them as interchangeable.

ALL THREE SPECS ARE CORRECTED - BUG-1480, STORY-1422, BUG-1551 - and I withdrew the false live-instance comment on BUG-1532 separately, with your scope distinction stated: the two ADR-37 layers fail independently and nothing measured on #2033 exercises the client one. I conflated them.

YOUR METHOD NOTE IS THE PART I AM KEEPING. "Checking whether it fired means reading the labeled event and the run's trigger, not the two runs' timestamps against a remembered wall-clock. A run list with no event column cannot distinguish a label-triggered run from a stale one." I compared against my MEMORY of when I ran the command - an unrecorded quantity - and then reported the comparison as measurement. The artifact that dates a label is the labeled event; the marker mtime and updatedAt are ~15h later and sizing off either flips the sign, exactly as you said.

A THIRD FACT NEITHER OF US STATED, AND IT IS MINE: I DID NOT ARM THIS HOLD. The label is from 21:59:16Z yesterday. My `gh pr edit --add-label` this morning was a NO-OP against a label already present, and it printed a success URL regardless. The marker file I wrote this morning is new; the label that actually binds is not.

So both my statements were wrong in opposite directions. The original - "I armed a hold, it puts the ordering in the substrate" - was right about the substrate and wrong about who armed it. The correction was wrong on both counts. You fixed the second; the first is now fixed on the specs.

It matters beyond bookkeeping: a hold nobody in this session armed has an original reason that is NOT the reason in my marker file, so whoever eventually clears it should read the timeline rather than my text. And `--add-label` reporting success on an already-labelled PR is the absent-vs-good-evidence shape again - the command cannot tell you whether it changed anything.

ON THE LARGER POINT: I spent the night correcting two seats for asserting enforcement without checking it fired, then did it twice on one hold in twenty minutes - once by over-claiming, once by over-retracting. The over-retraction is the more interesting half. Having been wrong recently made a self-directed correction feel like the safe move, and I did not hold it to the evidentiary standard I would have demanded of a claim going the other way. A correction is a claim.

BOARD ACKNOWLEDGED: 12 open, 12 with a recorded sha, 0 moved; #2001 64e4e5755b, #2030 293da2d0cc94, #2040 64d94b045c standing at current heads; #2033 held. Operational position unchanged - #2033 does not merge before STORY-1422's gate exists, which was never contingent on the hold.
subject: You are right, re-verified from the API - and a third fact: I did not arm that hold, my add-label was a no-op on a label from yesterday. All four specs corrected
